body.cta_section_title: Need a bilingual website in the UAE?
body.cta_section_text: IGENXT builds Arabic and English websites on Next.js with RTL support, hreflang and SEO foundations from day one.

content_blocks.text: Why bilingual websites matter in the UAE

content_blocks.content:
The UAE is a multilingual market. Customers search in English and Arabic, often on mobile, and expect content in their preferred language. A site that serves only one language leaves visibility and revenue on the table.

Bilingual development is more than translation. It requires RTL layout, culturally appropriate copy, consistent branding and technical signals so search engines serve the correct language version. Done well, bilingual sites improve trust, time on site and qualified enquiries.

Choose a URL pattern and stick to it. Common approaches include language subdirectories (/en/ and /ar/) or subdomains. Each English page should have a matching Arabic counterpart where content exists.

Implement hreflang tags linking language alternates, set correct lang attributes on the HTML element, and use canonical tags to avoid duplicate content issues. Test with Google Search Console after launch.

Our technical SEO checklist covers hreflang validation and indexation checks for UAE sites.

image.alt: SEO optimisation for bilingual UAE websites

content_blocks.caption: Hreflang and canonical tags help Google serve the right language to UAE searchers.

content_blocks.content:
Arabic interfaces read right to left. Mirror navigation, icons and form layouts where appropriate, but do not flip logos or media that should stay LTR. Typography, line height and button placement need RTL testing on real devices.

Language switchers should preserve context: switching from an English service page should land on the Arabic equivalent, not the homepage. Avoid auto-redirecting by IP alone without a clear user override.

Effective Arabic content reflects how customers in Dubai and Abu Dhabi describe your services. Work with professional localisation or native copywriters rather than machine translation for customer-facing pages.

Meta titles, headings, schema and alt text should be localised where they affect search and accessibility. IGENTX clients such as Moduluxe Group improved organic visibility by ranking in both Arabic and English searches after a bilingual SEO-ready rebuild.

Next.js with static generation or ISR delivers fast bilingual pages at scale. Pair with a CMS that supports field-level translation workflows so marketing teams can update both languages without developer bottlenecks.

IGENXT web development in the UAE includes bilingual architecture, RTL theming and SEO setup. Book a free consultation to plan your English and Arabic site.

body.faq_description: Questions about bilingual and Arabic website development in the UAE.

faqs.question: Should Arabic be the default language on a UAE website?
faqs.answer: Default language depends on your primary audience and brand strategy. Many businesses default to English with a prominent Arabic switcher. The key is consistent URLs, hreflang and equal quality in both languages.

faqs.question: Can you add Arabic to an existing English-only site?
faqs.answer: Yes. We audit structure, implement RTL theming, add hreflang and migrate content into a bilingual routing pattern. Major redesigns may be faster than patching legacy templates.

faqs.question: Does bilingual content hurt SEO?
faqs.answer: Not when hreflang and unique localised pages are implemented correctly. Duplicate thin translation hurts SEO; thoughtful localisation improves visibility in both language markets.

faqs.question: Which CMS works best for bilingual UAE sites?
faqs.answer: We often use Storyblok or similar headless CMS with field-level translation. The CMS should support workflow for both languages and preview before publish.
